stem.en: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of business?

options.en: Dealings in goods and services on a regular basis

explanation.en: Business returns are always uncertain; a guaranteed return is the opposite of 'uncertainty of return', which is a characteristic of business.

stem.en: A mother cooks food for her family at home. This is:

explanation.en: It is done out of love and affection, not to earn a living, so it is a non-economic activity.

stem.en: Ramesh sells his old personal scooter to a friend once. This is not a business activity mainly because:

options.en: No exchange of goods for money takes place
It involves no transfer of goods
It is not a dealing on a regular basis

explanation.en: A single, isolated sale is not business; business needs dealings in goods or services on a regular basis.

stem.en: In the indigenous banking system of ancient India, a 'hundi' was:

options.en: A tax collected from traders at city gates
An instrument of exchange used to transfer money and give credit, like a bill of exchange
A guild of merchants in a port town
A standard unit of weight for grain

explanation.en: Hundi was a financial instrument used by indigenous bankers for credit and transfer of funds, similar to a modern bill of exchange.

stem.en: The reward for a profession is:

explanation.en: Professionals such as doctors, lawyers and chartered accountants charge a professional fee for their services.

stem.en: Membership of a professional body and a certificate of practice are needed to start a:

explanation.en: A profession is entered by becoming a member of the professional body (e.g. Bar Council, ICAI) and getting a certificate of practice.

stem.en: In which economic activity is transfer of interest possible with some formalities?

explanation.en: A business can be sold or transferred; a profession or a job is personal and cannot be transferred.

stem.en: A qualified doctor works in a government hospital for a fixed monthly salary. She is engaged in:

explanation.en: Although she is a professional by qualification, here she works for an employer under a contract of service and earns a salary, so the activity is employment.

stem.en: In which economic activity is the risk lowest?

explanation.en: An employee gets a fixed and regular salary, so there is little or no risk; business profits are the most uncertain.

stem.en: An oil refinery separates crude oil into petrol, diesel and kerosene. This is an example of:

explanation.en: Analytical industry breaks one material into several useful products.

stem.en: Plant nurseries, cattle breeding farms and poultry farms belong to:

explanation.en: Genetic industries rear and multiply plants and animals for further reproduction or sale.

stem.en: Warehousing removes the hindrance of:

explanation.en: Goods produced at one time are stored until they are needed, so warehousing removes the hindrance of time.

stem.en: Which pair is correctly matched?

explanation.en: Cement is made by combining several materials, so it is synthetical. Mining and fishing are extractive (primary); sugar making is a processing industry.

stem.en: Importing goods only to re-export them to another country is called:

explanation.en: Entrepot trade (re-export) means importing goods for exporting them to other countries, possibly after some processing.

stem.en: Which of the following is NOT one of the multiple objectives of business described in NCERT?

options.en: Gaining a monopoly over the market

explanation.en: The objectives are market standing, innovation, productivity, physical and financial resources, earning profits, manager performance, worker performance and social responsibility. Monopoly is not one of them.

stem.en: 'Market standing' as an objective of business refers to:

options.en: The number of shops the firm owns
The position of an enterprise in relation to its competitors
The share price on a stock exchange

explanation.en: Market standing is the firm's standing relative to competitors; it must offer competitive products to serve customers to their satisfaction.

stem.en: Profit is needed by a business mainly because it:

options.en: Provides funds for expansion and growth
Replaces the need for social responsibility
Is required by law to be earned every year

explanation.en: Profit is a source of income, finance for expansion, a measure of efficiency and it builds reputation; it does not remove risk.

stem.en: Productivity as an objective is judged by comparing:

options.en: The profit of this year with last year
The number of workers with the number of managers
The value of output with the value of inputs

explanation.en: Productivity is the ratio of output to input; a business must keep improving it to survive and grow.

stem.en: A firm sets up a research cell to develop new products and new methods of production. Which objective is it pursuing?

explanation.en: Innovation means introducing new ideas or methods in the way of doing business.

stem.en: Profit is regarded as the reward for:

explanation.en: No business can avoid risk; the entrepreneur bears it and profit is the reward for bearing it.

stem.en: A strike by employees that stops production is which cause of business risk?

explanation.en: Human causes include dishonesty, carelessness, strikes, riots and management inefficiency.

stem.en: A fall in demand for a product because of a change in fashion is a/an:

explanation.en: Economic causes include changes in demand, competition, prices and technology.

stem.en: Which statement about business risk is NOT correct?

options.en: Business risks arise due to uncertainties
Risk is an essential part of every business
Risk can be completely eliminated by careful planning
The degree of risk depends mainly on the nature and size of business

explanation.en: Risk can be reduced but never fully eliminated; it is an essential part of every business.

stem.en: Which of the following is the first basic factor to decide when starting a business?

options.en: Selection of the line of business

explanation.en: The entrepreneur first decides the kind and nature of business to start; the size, form, location, finance, layout and tax planning follow.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): A teacher working in a private school is engaged in employment and not in a profession.
Reason (R): In employment a person works for others under a contract of service and receives a salary.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: The teacher works for an employer for a salary, which is exactly what makes it employment. R explains A.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Warehousing is an auxiliary to trade.
Reason (R): Warehousing removes the hindrance of place.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Warehousing is an auxiliary to trade, but it removes the hindrance of time; transport removes the hindrance of place.

stem.en: The flood that spoilt Nisha's stock is which cause of business risk?

explanation.en: Floods, earthquakes and heavy rains are natural causes beyond human control.

passage.en: Nisha runs a bakery in Hubballi. She buys flour from a mill, pays a transport company to bring it, keeps extra sugar in a rented godown and has insured her shop against fire. Last month heavy rains flooded the shop and spoilt stock worth ₹40,000. Two of her workers also left without notice in the festival season, and a new bakery opened next door offering lower prices.

stem.en: The new bakery next door offering lower prices is an example of:

options.en: A natural cause of business risk
An economic cause of business risk
A human cause of business risk

explanation.en: Competition and price changes are economic causes of business risk.

passage.en: Nisha runs a bakery in Hubballi. She buys flour from a mill, pays a transport company to bring it, keeps extra sugar in a rented godown and has insured her shop against fire. Last month heavy rains flooded the shop and spoilt stock worth ₹40,000. Two of her workers also left without notice in the festival season, and a new bakery opened next door offering lower prices.

stem.en:
Match List I (auxiliary to trade) with List II (hindrance removed):
A. Warehousing  B. Insurance  C. Banking  D. Advertising
I. Risk  II. Finance  III. Information  IV. Time

explanation.en: Warehousing removes the hindrance of time, insurance of risk, banking of finance and advertising of information.

stem.en:
Arrange the following basic factors in starting a business in the correct order:
A. Selection of form of ownership
B. Selection of the line of business
C. Location of the business
D. Launching the enterprise

explanation.en: The entrepreneur first selects the line of business, then the form of ownership, then the location, and launches the enterprise last.

stem.en:
Which of the following are genetic industries?
A. Poultry farm
B. Fish hatchery
C. Coal mining
D. Cement manufacture
E. Plant nursery

explanation.en: Genetic industries rear and multiply plants and animals: poultry farms, fish hatcheries and nurseries. Coal mining is extractive and cement is manufacturing.
